source: Aria Networks — Closing conversation: Deep Networking and token economics; Aria vs Arista's rise in the cloud era; NeoCloud and accelerator vendors
summary: Coreweave's networking investment is the core source of its competitive advantage and premium pricing power
summary_extended: Baker argues that Coreweave's (CRWV) primary competitive moat and the structural reason it commands a premium price per GPU hour relative to all other NeoCloud providers is its disproportionately high investment in networking infrastructure. He explains that superior networking translates directly into more effective FLOPS delivered per GPU hour, meaning customers get meaningfully better compute utilization for the same nominal GPU count — a tangible performance advantage that justifies premium pricing. Baker grounds this view in a long-standing personal relationship with Coreweave's founder Corey, citing direct conversations in which Coreweave's own leadership identifies networking investment as the definitive answer to 'why are you good?' The investment implication is that CRWV's networking-driven performance advantage is durable and structural, not easily replicated by competing NeoCloud operators, supporting a medium-term long position in CRWV as the premium-priced leader in the NeoCloud segment.
detail: Baker explains that Coreweave's ability to charge a higher price per GPU hour than any other NeoCloud stems directly from its superior networking investment, which delivers more effective FLOPS per GPU hour. This is the structural moat in the NeoCloud business.
confidence_evidence: Baker is a disclosed Coreweave shareholder and cites direct conversations with Coreweave's founder ('I've known Corey for a long time'). He frames this as the definitive answer to 'why are you good?'

ticker_audit.reasoning: The thesis is specifically and entirely about Coreweave's networking investment as the source of its competitive moat and premium pricing power. CRWV is the direct subject.
